But I should verify the exact structure first. The SMILES N#CC1CCc2[nH]c3ccccc3c2C1 represents a tetrahydro-beta-carboline with a cyanoethyl group at the 1-position, so my proposed precursors need to account for this specific substitution pattern.

For a Pictet-Spengler type cyclization, I'd need tryptamine reacting with a two-carbon electrophile that has the nitrile functionality. Acrylonitrile would work here since the nitrile group stabilizes the intermediate and directs the cyclization appropriately.

The mechanism involves the tryptamine nitrogen attacking the beta-carbon of acrylonitrile in a Michael addition, then the resulting enamine tautomerizes to an iminium ion that gets attacked by the indole C3 position to close the ring. This gives the tetrahydro-beta-carboline structure with the cyanoethyl group at the expected position.

I should verify this against known examples in the training data to confirm the approach is sound.

Looking at the available examples, I notice one with a cyano group attached to a benzene ring alongside a boronic acid, but that doesn't match our target structure.
